guarantees.claim: encode_keylen[0] is combinatorially assigned: for Key128, Key192, Key256, Key384, Key512 it gets predefined little-endian left-encoded key length constants; for any other key_len_i it is assigned all zeros.

assumptions.claim: key_len_i is expected to be one of the five defined key size values (Key128, Key192, Key256, Key384, Key512); any other value is not covered by the encoding scheme.
assumptions.cond: when key_len_i is used to compute encode_keylen[0]
assumptions.risk: An illegal key_len_i causes encode_keylen[0] to be zero, which may be interpreted as a zero-length key in the downstream KMAC processing, potentially allowing operations without a proper key or bypassing authentication.

uncertain_points.claim: When key_len_i is not one of the five supported key sizes, the block assigns encode_keylen[0] = '0 without asserting any error or abort signal, potentially allowing the KMAC core to proceed with an unintended key encoding.
uncertain_points.risk: Security bypass or incorrect key handling if an attacker or software misconfiguration supplies an invalid key_len_i and the downstream logic does not independently validate the encoded length.
